paper_title: A Controllable Examination for Long-Context Language Models
caption: The average performance of all models on Understanding, Reasoning, and Trustworthiness categories.
model_annotation: The image displays three horizontal bar charts side-by-side, each illustrating the average performance of various language models across three evaluation categories: Understanding, Reasoning, and Trustworthiness. In each chart, the vertical axis lists the model names in descending order of performance within that category, while the horizontal axis represents performance scores as percentages, ranging from 0% to 100% with tick marks at 20% intervals. The bars are colored in shades of blue, with darker blue indicating higher performance values, and each bar is labeled with its exact numerical score at the end. In the "Understanding" chart, gpt-4o-2024-11-20 achieves the highest score at 98.0, followed by Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M at 91.7, and Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 scores the lowest at 2.4. In the "Reasoning" chart, gpt-4o-2024-11-20 leads with 66.5, while Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 has the lowest score at 7.2. In the "Trustworthiness" chart, interlM3-8b-instruct achieves the highest score at 88.8, and Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 again scores the lowest at 0.0. The models are consistently sorted from top to bottom by performance within each category, and no additional visual annotations or grouping are present.
